title: A rare—important Violin by: Gio. Paolo Maggini, bearing the maker's label: GIO PAOLO MAGGINI IN BREFCIA. With the certificate of MESSRS. W. E. HILL & SONS, London, dated June 1941. Stating: The Violin was made by GIO. PAOLO MAGGINI whose original label the instrument bears. It dates from circa 1610-15. The back in one-piece, is of wood cut on the slab and marked by a faint horizontal curl, that of the sides and head cut on the quarter, by a more pronounced curl, the table is of pine of well defined and open grain and the varnish of a golden brown colour. This violin, which is double purfled and of its original dimensions, 14⁷/₁₆in. (367mm.), is in a fine state of preservation (see accompanying letter). With a fine fitted figured rosewood case and cover by W. E. HILL & SONS. Extracts from letter reads, "A fine example of the maker's work, its original proportions being intact—a feature one rarely comes across and similar to the DUMAS MAGGINI referred to in our Life of the maker." Mention of great players who have preferred MAGGINI instruments. It was purchased by MR. ALFRED HILL from H. C. SILVESTRE of Paris in the early part of this century.
